- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3 days, model often misjudges direction; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and use sentiment median as anchor.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mean price; apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67).
- If sentiment is high and price is near recent 10-day high, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is high but price is trending sideways; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.67 and price <10-day moving average.
